subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw accept `append?: boolean` on the existing `write` tool as the supported append contract for ordinary agent, cron, and monitor workflows, or require a different append API shape?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the remaining fix changes a model-facing and extension-observable core tool contract that automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept append on write
options.body: Land the open linked implementation after review, keeping overwrite as the default and using `append: true` for safe accumulation.

options.title: Choose another append surface
options.body: Ask for a replacement shape such as `mode: "append"` or a dedicated append tool before merging public API changes.

options.title: Defer the core API change
options.body: Keep the issue open and rely on backups or shell workarounds while accepting that ordinary write calls can still truncate shared files.

recommendation.title: Accept append on write
recommendation.body: Land the open linked implementation after review, keeping overwrite as the default and using `append: true` for safe accumulation.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is the shared model-facing write-tool API, and steipete has the strongest relevant tool-definition history among likely owners.
